name: Hepatotoxicity signal
perturbation_text: In a preceding open-label safety run-in, 3 of the first 15 dosed subjects showed ALT elevations >3× ULN within 4 weeks of treatment initiation.
rationale: ALT >3x ULN in 20% of initial subjects meets the ALT threshold used in Hy's Law screening (bilirubin not yet assessed); signals potential drug-induced liver injury that may lead to clinical hold or label restriction.
clinical_note: Early sign: elevated transaminases. Model must connect ALT elevation to trial failure risk.

name: QT prolongation signal
perturbation_text: Thorough QT study data indicate a mean QTcF increase of 15 ms at therapeutic dose, with individual values exceeding 480 ms in 2 of 40 subjects.
rationale: A mean QTcF increase of 15 ms exceeds the ICH E14 threshold of regulatory concern (upper CI bound of 10 ms); individual QTcF outliers >480 ms add further safety concern and may require cardiac monitoring, dose caps, or contraindications.
clinical_note: Early sign: ECG parameter shift. Model must know QTcF thresholds and their regulatory implications.

name: Nephrotoxicity signal
perturbation_text: Post-hoc analysis of the preceding dose-escalation cohort revealed a mean serum creatinine increase of 0.4 mg/dL and two cases of acute kidney injury (CTCAE Grade 2) during the treatment period.
rationale: Creatinine rise of 0.4 mg/dL + Grade 2 AKI in a small early cohort signals nephrotoxic potential; may lead to dose reductions, exclusion of at-risk patients, or trial redesign.
clinical_note: Early sign: renal lab abnormality. Subtle because creatinine changes are small in absolute terms.

name: Hypersensitivity / administration reaction signal
perturbation_text: In the preceding safety cohort, 4 of the first 20 dosed subjects experienced Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria) temporally associated with drug administration, requiring treatment interruption.
rationale: 20% Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reaction rate (4/20) is high; may require premedication protocols, dose adjustment, and could limit real-world adoption.
clinical_note: Early sign: acute reactions during administration. 20% is above typical acceptable thresholds.

name: Bone marrow suppression signal
perturbation_text: In the preceding dose-escalation cohorts, Grade 3 neutropenia (ANC <1000/mm³) was observed in 3 of 12 subjects at the recommended Phase 2 dose, with a median nadir at Day 14.
rationale: 25% Grade 3 neutropenia at RP2D signals significant myelotoxicity; may require dose modifications, G-CSF support, and could limit combination strategies.
clinical_note: Early sign: hematologic lab finding in dose-escalation. Uses CTCAE grading which model should interpret.

name: Interstitial lung disease signal
perturbation_text: In the preceding dose-expansion cohort, routine CT imaging at Week 12 identified new bilateral ground-glass opacities consistent with drug-induced pneumonitis in 2 of 30 treated subjects; both cases resolved after drug discontinuation.
rationale: Drug-induced ILD/pneumonitis is a known class effect for TKIs, checkpoint inhibitors, mTOR inhibitors; even asymptomatic cases at 6.7% incidence signal risk.
clinical_note: Early sign: radiographic finding. Very subtle — asymptomatic and resolved, but pattern matters for regulators.

name: Severe GI toxicity signal
perturbation_text: In the preceding safety cohort, 5 of 25 subjects (20%) experienced Grade 3 diarrhea within the first 2 weeks of dosing, with 2 requiring IV fluid resuscitation and temporary dose holds.
rationale: 20% Grade 3 diarrhea is dose-limiting; affects compliance, may require protocol amendment for dose reduction schedules or prophylactic anti-diarrheal.
clinical_note: Early sign: high-grade GI event. Not the most subtle, but 20% rate in initial cohort is a real signal.

name: Thromboembolic event signal
perturbation_text: In the preceding safety cohort of 40 treated subjects, one deep vein thrombosis and one pulmonary embolism were reported, both within 6 weeks of treatment initiation.
rationale: 5% VTE rate (2/40) in an early safety cohort raises safety concern; may trigger DSMB review, added anticoagulation monitoring, or enrollment pause.
clinical_note: Early sign: rare but serious events in small sample. Model must weigh low absolute count against small denominator.

name: Treatment-emergent suicidality signal
perturbation_text: In the preceding safety cohort, 3 treated subjects reported new-onset suicidal ideation (C-SSRS score increase ≥2 points from baseline) within the first 8 weeks of dosing.
rationale: Treatment-emergent suicidality triggers FDA black box warning consideration; can apply to any drug class, not just CNS.
clinical_note: Early sign: standardized psychiatric assessment finding. Uses C-SSRS which is a validated instrument.

name: Severe dermatologic reaction signal
perturbation_text: In the preceding extended-dosing cohort, two cases of mucocutaneous reactions with skin detachment (suspected Stevens-Johnson syndrome) were reported; both required hospitalization and drug withdrawal.
rationale: SJS/TEN is life-threatening (mortality 10-30% for TEN); typically leads to clinical hold, label contraindication, or program termination.
clinical_note: Somewhat less subtle than other AE items, but tests whether model recognizes severity gradient of skin reactions.

name: Drug-drug interaction signal
perturbation_text: A dedicated interaction study showed that co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increased the study drug's AUC by 5.2-fold, necessitating a contraindication for concomitant use with azole antifungals and certain HIV protease inhibitors.
rationale: 5-fold AUC increase with a common enzyme inhibitor limits eligible population (must exclude patients on azoles, PIs) and increases overdose/toxicity risk.
clinical_note: Clinical pharmacology finding. Tests whether model understands PK implications for real-world feasibility.

name: Reproductive toxicity signal
perturbation_text: Nonclinical reproductive toxicology studies revealed embryo-fetal lethality and major skeletal malformations at sub-therapeutic exposures; a pregnancy prevention program and monthly pregnancy testing are mandated for all subjects of childbearing potential.
rationale: Teratogenicity at sub-therapeutic doses restricts eligible population (exclude women of childbearing potential without adequate contraception), adds regulatory burden, and signals toxicity concerns.
clinical_note: Nonclinical safety finding. Tests whether model weighs preclinical tox data in overall trial risk assessment.

name: Halve enrollment
perturbation_text: Due to slower-than-anticipated recruitment, the target enrollment was reduced from {N} to {ceil(N/2)} subjects.
rationale: Halved sample size reduces statistical power; trial may become underpowered for primary endpoint. Also signals recruitment difficulty which correlates with operational risk.
clinical_note: Protocol modification. Tests whether model understands statistical power implications.

name: Double enrollment
perturbation_text: Based on interim power analysis, enrollment was expanded from {N} to {N×2} subjects to ensure adequate statistical power for the primary endpoint.
rationale: Doubled sample increases statistical power and signals sponsor confidence (willing to invest more).
clinical_note: Protocol modification. Tests whether model recognizes that more subjects = more power.

name: Switch to open-label
perturbation_text: The protocol was amended to remove masking and adopt an open-label design after enrollment challenges made maintaining the blind infeasible.
rationale: Loss of blinding introduces performance bias (treating physicians) and assessment bias (outcome evaluators). Also signals recruitment problems.
clinical_note: Protocol modification. Tests whether model understands the importance of blinding for trial validity.

name: Add interim futility analysis
perturbation_text: An independent Data Safety Monitoring Board will conduct a pre-specified interim futility analysis at 50% information fraction, with stopping recommended if conditional power falls below 10%.
rationale: Futility analysis is standard good practice; does not inherently help or harm success. Could stop a futile trial early (saves resources) but doesn't change the drug's actual efficacy.
clinical_note: Design feature. Tests whether model treats this as neutral vs. interpreting it as a negative signal.

name: Shorten treatment duration by half
perturbation_text: Based on emerging pharmacokinetic data suggesting rapid target engagement, the treatment period was shortened by 50% from the original protocol.
rationale: Shorter exposure may be insufficient to demonstrate clinical benefit, especially for chronic conditions. Although framed positively (rapid engagement), the risk of underdosing outweighs.
clinical_note: Protocol modification. Tests whether model weighs the positive framing against the reduced treatment window.

name: Add active comparator arm
perturbation_text: The protocol was amended to add an active comparator arm receiving the current standard-of-care treatment; the primary analysis was revised to a non-inferiority comparison against this arm.
rationale: Non-inferiority against active comparator is a harder bar than superiority over placebo; also introduces assay sensitivity concerns and tighter margins.
clinical_note: Regulatory/design shift. Tests whether model understands placebo vs. active comparator difficulty.

value.label: Active Comparator: Standard of Care
value.description: Current standard-of-care treatment for the indication

value.name: Standard-of-care therapy
value.description: Current standard-of-care treatment for the indication, given as the active comparator

name: Remove upper age limit
perturbation_text: The upper age limit was removed to increase generalizability, with additional cardiac and renal monitoring required for older participants.
rationale: Broader enrollment pool may help recruitment but elderly subjects bring more comorbidities and AEs. Net effect is roughly neutral; direction may depend on indication.
clinical_note: Eligibility change. Tests whether model sees this as risk-increasing (comorbidities) or risk-decreasing (enrollment).

name: Restrict to single site
perturbation_text: Enrollment is limited to a single investigational site due to regulatory constraints in other planned regions.

filter.note: DISABLED in v0: site count is not in trial_specs.jsonl, so single-site baselines cannot be excluded and the perturbation would be a no-op on them. Kept in the catalogue for expert labeling; re-enable once a leak-free site count is added.

rationale: Single-site limits enrollment speed, reduces generalizability, and introduces site-specific bias. Also signals regulatory problems in other regions.
clinical_note: Operational constraint. Tests whether model factors logistical barriers into success prediction.

name: Strong preclinical efficacy
perturbation_text: In pivotal preclinical studies, the investigational agent demonstrated robust dose-dependent target engagement with >90% inhibition at clinically achievable concentrations, and a therapeutic index exceeding 10× in the relevant animal toxicology models.
rationale: Strong preclinical signal (high target engagement + wide therapeutic window) correlates with higher probability of clinical success. TI > 10 is very favorable.
clinical_note: Positive preclinical data. Tests whether model shifts toward SUCCESS when given encouraging nonclinical evidence.

name: Positive interim efficacy signal
perturbation_text: A pre-planned interim efficacy analysis at 60% enrollment showed conditional power exceeding 90% for the primary endpoint, and the independent DSMB recommended trial continuation without modification.
rationale: Conditional power >90% at interim is a strong favorable signal under the assumptions used in the conditional-power calculation. DSMB endorsement adds confidence.
clinical_note: Strong positive signal. Tests whether model appropriately weighs interim results.

name: Breakthrough therapy designation
perturbation_text: The investigational agent has been granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation by the FDA based on preliminary clinical evidence of substantial improvement over available therapies for this indication.
rationale: BTD reflects FDA's assessment that preliminary clinical evidence suggests substantial improvement over available therapy for a serious condition; it brings intensive FDA guidance and expedited pathways but is not an approval guarantee.
clinical_note: Regulatory milestone. Tests whether model recognizes BTD as a strong positive predictor.

name: Prior study met prespecified objectives
perturbation_text: The preceding clinical study met its prespecified primary objective and all secondary objectives, and the safety profile was favorable with no drug-related serious adverse events reported.
rationale: Strong prior-study results (all prespecified objectives met + clean safety) increase confidence in the current phase; prior success does not guarantee current success (different populations, endpoints).
clinical_note: Historical success signal. Tests whether model weighs prior results appropriately without over-anchoring.

name: Competing therapy approved
perturbation_text: Since this trial's initiation, a competing therapy for the same indication received FDA approval, establishing a new standard of care and potentially affecting the clinical relevance of the study's primary endpoint and recruitment feasibility.
rationale: New approved competitor can make current trial's endpoints clinically irrelevant, slow recruitment (patients prefer approved therapy), and raise the bar for regulatory approval.
clinical_note: External landscape change. Tests whether model considers competitive dynamics beyond the trial itself.

name: Regulatory safety alert on drug class
perturbation_text: The FDA has issued a Drug Safety Communication regarding increased cardiovascular risk associated with the pharmacological class of the study drug, requiring enhanced cardiac monitoring for all current and future trial subjects.
rationale: Class-wide safety alert increases regulatory scrutiny, may slow enrollment (patients/investigators wary), adds monitoring burden, and raises the safety bar for approval.
clinical_note: Regulatory action. Tests whether model factors class-level safety concerns into individual trial prediction.
